title: Fighting for Tskhinvali ends and each side reports casualties
body:
The fighting for Tskhinvali ran from 8 to 11 August 2008. Georgian troops entered the city early on 8 August and withdrew on the evening of 10 August, when Georgia announced a unilateral ceasefire; most Georgian troops had left South Ossetia by the night of 10-11 August. The European Union fact-finding mission counted 10,000 to 11,000 Georgian servicemen in South Ossetia, while South Ossetian forces numbered up to 3,500.

Casualty figures differ by source. The Georgian Ministry of Defence reported 169 killed, 947 wounded and 1 missing, and the Georgian Ministry of Internal Affairs reported 11 killed, 227 wounded and 3 missing. For Russia, RIA Novosti reported in 2009 that 67 servicemen were killed, while Reuters reported 283 wounded and 3 missing. The South Ossetian Ministry of Defence reported 27 killed and 69 wounded, and its Interior Ministry reported 10 killed.

Russian authorities initially claimed up to 2,000 civilian deaths by 9 August 2008. In December 2008 Russia's Investigative Committee revised the figure to 162 South Ossetian casualties. The Wikipedia article states that Russia's genocide accusation against Georgia was unsupported. On 12 August Russian President Dmitry Medvedev said military action would stop because "the aggressor has been punished".
